text: Heavy Leggings L are heavy legs armour in . They can be purchased from shops for 27,800 G.
Heavy Armours L are heavy torso armour in . They can be purchased from shops for 34,800 G.

Hadron Impact (Japanese: , Higgusuinpakuto) is Addam and Mythra's Level IV Blade Special in . It is unlocked once the party sets off for Auresco. If Hadron Impact is activated by Addam, the special's element will be determined by the Greatsword he has equipped.
Hailstrike (Japanese: , Hisame, "Freezing Rain") is Jin's Level I Blade Special in .
Heaven on Earth (Japanese: ) is Herald's Level IV Blade Special in .
Heliodor Passion (Japanese: ) is Agate's Level I Blade Special in .
Hellbound (Japanese: , Herubaundo) is Wulfric's Level III Blade Special in .
Hellwind of Ruin (Japanese: ) is Akhos's Level IV Blade Special in .

Haze's Talisman-making is a skill in , with which Haze can prepare Talisman Pouch items from various Collectibles at campsites. These recipes and items are unique to Haze and cannot be obtained any other way. Recipes are unlocked by receiving them as rewards for certain Quests. Haze is the only character who can craft Talismans.
Heavy Guard (Japanese: , Hevi Gādo) is a Kevesi Defender class in .
Hanassa Amoneys (Japanese: , Hanasa Amonē) are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Amoney family, and can be found at level 29-30 in Amoney's Hallows at Great Cotte Falls.
Hammer Revolution (Japanese: , Hanmāreboryūshon) is Sena's Ouroboros Talent Art in .
Hazy Figure (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Tactician class.

Hero Quests are a type of quest in involving Heroes. They are similar to Blade Quests in . Completing a Hero Quest unlocks a Hero to be usable in the party, and unlocks their class for Ouroboros. Ascension Quests are Hero Quests that, upon completion, will increase the maximum Class Rank for corresponding Hero's class from 10 to 20. Additionally, six Side Story Quests will similarly increase the maximum rank for the base class corresponding to the party member it features. In order to be started, Ascension Quests require at least one party member to be at rank 10 with the hero's class, for the relevant hero to be in the party, and for the hero's questline to be sufficiently progressed.
The Heat Gauge (Japanese: , hītogēji) is a battle mechanic in .
Harala is a Nopon NPC in who can be found in Colony 9. __TOC__

Hazardous Jarrahed (Japanese: , Kinan no Jaraheddo) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Aspar family, and can be found at level 16 at Racine's Platter in Eagus Wilderness, south of Galghour's Menhir. The Snake Eyes Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Hedonist Tirkin (Japanese: , Yuraku no Tākin) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 23 at the Tirkin Headquarters in Ribbi Flats. The Tactical Eye Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class for defeating it.
Hangar, Lower: East Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Kasō Higashi Gēto) is a Landmark in . It is located on the first floor of Keves Castle.
Hangar, Lower: West Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Kasō Nishi Gēto) is a Landmark in . It is located on the first floor of Keves Castle.
Hangar, Lower Level (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Kasō) is a Location in . It is located on the first floor of Keves Castle.
The Hangar, Passageway (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Renrakutsūro) is a Location in . It is located on the first floor of Keves Castle.
The Hangar, Upper: Main Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Jōsō Chūō Gēto) is a Landmark in . It is located on the second floor of Keves Castle.
Hangar, Upper Level (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Jōsō) is a Location in . It is located on the second floor of Keves Castle.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Heavy Weak Guards are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Colony 30 Commissary. The legendary variant can be purchased at the Prize X-change Red. In , the common variant can be purchased from the Colony 9 Supply Office.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Herald's Kneeguards are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Tableland Caravan and Tunnel Caravan. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Bombastic Rotbart Jr..

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Hermit Masks are Accessories in and . The legendary variant can be obtained from Farseer Pirtett. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Fograptor D'nari.
Hegemon's Seat (Japanese: , Hasha no Bōrō) is a Landmark in . It is located above Lake Rezzento in the Eagus Wilderness in the Fornis Region.
The Headwater Camp (Japanese: , Suigen no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located at the Great Sword's Base in the Cadensia Region.
Hermit's Inlet (Japanese: , Inja no Irie) is a Landmark in . It is located in Erythia Sea. The entrance into Farlaine Underpass, which opens up during Side Story: Taion, is located here.
The Hargan Point Camp (Japanese: , Hāgan-misaki no Kyūsokuchi) is a Rest Spot in . It is located at Hargan Point in Erythia Sea.
Hargan Point (Japanese: , Hāgan-misaki) is a Location in . It is located in Erythia Sea. Colony 15 is located here.

Heavy Pomegranates are Collectibles in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region on Twinpalm Isle, in Agnus Castle Barbican and on the Bed of Woes and Wishes. They may also be obtained from the fabricator at the Atoll Ferronis Hulk. Twenty are needed for Shock to the System.

The Hall of the Serene (Japanese: , Yūgen no Ma) is a Landmark in , located in the Cloudkeep on Captocorn Peak. It is where the party meets Nia and learns about the Origin and the story behind the creation of Aionios. There is a supercomputer located here that Poppi is inside. After completing the story, Nia can be unlocked as a Hero by returning here.

Heretical Saurow (Japanese: , Itan no Sauro) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Upa family, and can be found at level 25 at Old Kana Battlefield on Rae-Bel Tableland. The Hypno-Light Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Hardscale Gouran (Japanese: , Gōrin no Kōraru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Merigna family, and can be found at level 66 at Oshia's Reef Ravine in Erythia Sea. It forms the trio "Whirlpool Triumvirate" with Sharpscale Ragoon and Fairscale Marina. The Dragon Decree Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Hardshelled Admory (Japanese: , Gankaku no Adomarī) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Krammit family, and can be found at level 57 at the Krezen Cliffs in Erythia Sea. The Shell Guard Art can be earned by the Soulhacker class for defeating it.

Heavenrazor Egreet (Japanese: , Shōten no Iguretto) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 90 in The Cavity. The Gatling Peck Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

The Heroic Gulkin (Japanese: , Giyū no Hākin) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Gulkin family, and can be found at level 76 at the Place of Heroes Past in Erythia Sea, accessible after entering Origin for the first time. The Royal Charisma Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
The Helheim Sky Bridge (Japanese: , Hiruheimu Renrakutsūro) is a Location in . It is located at Fort O'Virbus on the Syra Hovering Reefs.

|-|Attacker= |-|Defender= |-|Healer= Harmonic Wave (Japanese: ,Hāmonikusuweibu) is one of Noah's Arts with Lucky Seven in . The effects of this art change depending on the Role of Noah's current class. This art is unlocked after defeating N in the Eternal Prison in the Origin Interior. In order to use this art, Noah must first use the Unlimited Sword Talent Art.
The Hangar, Lower: Main Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Kasō Chūō Gēto) is a Landmark in , located in the Origin Interior. The Unique Monster Desired Oruria is found here.
Hangar, Upper: East Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Jōsō Higashi Gēto) is a Landmark in , located in the Origin Interior.
Hangar, Upper: West Gate (Japanese: , Kakunōko: Jōsō Nishi Gēto) is a Landmark in , located in the Origin Interior.
The Hangar Zone (Japanese: , Kakunōko Kukaku) is a Location in , located in the Origin Interior. Monica and Ghondor rejoin the party as Heroes after defeating the Kurria Flak ambush that occurs here.
Helping Out is a Standard Quest in . After this quest is completed, No Want of Courage will be automatically accepted.
Her Reasons (Japanese: , Mada Minu Keshiki) is a Hero Quest in , dedicated to Alexandria.
Happiness (Japanese: , Shiawase) is an Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Miyabi.
Helix Conches are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. They can also be produced from the Clifftop Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Harmony Ebonies are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. They can also be produced from the Clifftop Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Heartkiller Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 45 at the Igna Conglomerate on Elaice Highway, or at level 99 in Rebellion Cave in Erythia Sea.
Heavy-Duty Firelighters are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Hadron Units are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Origin. They can also be produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator after reaching Origin for the first time.
Hemish Krodlax are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Krodlax family, and can be found at level 58 at Cape Arcaphor and at level 61-62 south of Irma's Secret Base in Erythia Sea.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Hellfire Amulets are Accessories in and . The legendary variant can be obtained from Diabolical Rindolph.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Harness Belts are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Battlescar Caravan, and the legendary variant can be obtained from Otherworldly Rodsin.
Handypon is a shop in . It is an Accessory shop run by Wheelideeli in the Central Cell of Li Garte Prison Camp after completing Prison Refurbishment.
Heewa's Belongings is a Key Item in . It is a hair tie that belonged to Heewa, and it is found in the Gura Flava Lowlands in Alfeto Valley during Vandham's Heir.
The Harvest Day Tiara is a Key Item in . Chickadee asks for the party to give the tiara to Misaka during Harvest Day.

Hedred Scorpoxes are five Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Scorpox family that are fought alongside the Ribeega Scorpox at level 48 at the Apex Wing in the Dannagh Desert during Beyond Mercy and Revenge.
Heavy Armus are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Armu family, and can be found at level 45 in Erythia Sea in the Cadensia Region.

Heewa is an NPC in . She was a member of the Lost Numbers under Guernica Vandham's squad alongside Yew and Zuo. Like the other members of her squad, she was killed in action at Gura Flava Lowlands in an attempt to prevent their adversaries from obtaining the Ouroboros Stone, although she is never explicitly shown to be on screen. Her sister is Cyma, one of the Ouroboros candidates.
The Hantis Ansel is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Ansel family, and is fought at level 46 at Magglia Lake at Ribbi Flats during Rules of the Hunt.
Havoc Slayer is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Machine Assassin class.

Heroes Frontline (Japanese: , Eiyū Sensen) is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will reward the player with an Accomplished Necklace.

Heavenly Spear (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Inferno Dance that can only be used by Cammuravi. He uses his fiery lance to catapult himself into the air and launches his lance at an enemy at the expense of some damage.

Hard Dig is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Sycophantic Lilith while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Hawk Shot (Japanese: , Lit. "Hawk Missile") is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Terrorbird Zieger while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Healing Rest is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Timbercorn Cthinos while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.
Heal Bind is a Status Effect in . It only affects Healers and prevents them from taking any actions during the effect.

Hamill is an NPC in . He is the younger brother of Lucille and a member of the Liberators in Colony 9. Hamill's Community is gained after talking to him three times, completing The Running Automaton, and starting Chapter 4.

Harby is an NPC in . He is a former Agnus soldier who now works for the Liberators in Colony 9. Harby's Community is gained when talking to him after completing Where Is That Guy? and then talking with him.
Hard Eggshells are items in . They can be dropped by Aspar Eggs in Aurora Shelf.

Heart in the Fog is a track from , composed by Manami Kiyota. It is track nine of disc five from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track nine of disc ten from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * The party regroups after being swallowed by the Urayan Titan. * When Nia notices that Pyra left the inn in Fonsa Myma. * During the flashback of Nia becoming a Flesh Eater and awakening Dromarch. * When Jin reveals the Blades that perished during the process of becoming Titans within Torna's matrix. * Rex's encounter with the phantasm of Nia and Dromarch in the First Low Orbit Station. * When Azami uses her Clairvoyant Eye during All's

|-|Chapter 8= |-|Challenge Battle Mode= Heavenly Disrupt (Japanese: , Tenranken, "Heavenly Disturbance Sword") is a Battle Art in . It is one of Jin's arts as a temporary party member during Chapter 8, and during the Challenge Battle Titan Battleship Assault.
Hammer Bash (Japanese: , Hanmābasshu) is a Battle Art used by Malos in . Malos bashes the enemy with the weapon in its "shield form".

Hekasa's Stake is a Key Item in . It is a stake that Hekasa gives to the party during Hekasa's Labour at Stake for the purpose of planting it on the lakeshore by the Junks. It is later stolen by the Ramrod Tirkin.
Heroic Tale is one of Neilnail's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn it by completing The Custodian's Duty.
Hammurabi, the Transgressor (Japanese: , Gōma no Hamurabi) is a Tyrant in . It is a member of the Milsaadi family. It can be found at level 54 in Volitaris.
Hercules Blow is one of Al's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn it by completing One Big Happy Family.
Heart of the Warrior is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in front of the "NLA Food Market" on North Founders Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles between Ga Jiarg and Cross.
Heal Familivs are Story Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Familiv family, and can be found at level 59 inside the Tower of Eternity on Volitaris after being summoned by Void.
The Heart Stone is an Important Item in . It is collected on the Floating Reef in Oblivia during the course of Straight from the Heart.
Harula is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found at Fonsa Myma Port in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Hamoosh is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found in Jarlin, Wing Area #1 in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

Haze Milsaadi (Japanese: , Heizu Mirusādo) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Milsaadi Ganglion soldiers. They can be found at levels 41-49 on Northern Searoad in Sylvalum during White Lifehold, and are fought in two successive battles.
Heathorns are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Cetos, Tornado Claw type Galdrs or black Puges.

Helehele is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found outside the Chairman's Room in the Argentum Trade Guild. She stands on a desk to the left of the Chairman's doorway, watching the comings and goings of the people who consult with him. She shares gossip about the goings-on of Argentum's politics with the party. She offers the Merc Mission Ship Snooping.
Havard is an NPC in . Havard is an Urayan who can be found in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. Havard runs a shop called Volty Butchers specialized in Meats.
Homs (English dub: ) are a form of life indigenous to the Bionis, and the main playable race in . They are analogous to humans. The Nopon call them Hom Hom ().

Hover Astas are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Astas family, and can be found at level 33 in the halls near the Tomb Robber Pool and between the Valley of Emperors and the Tower of Trials - Bridge in the High Entia Tomb. Shulk and the party face it as one of the basic types of enemies. As with all of the monsters in the High Entia Tomb, it is a Sight Category monster. They can drop Astas Remote Units, which are needed for A Necessary Upgrade. They can also drop the New Cylinders needed for Restoring the Capital 2. A variant Hover Astas appears only during a story event battle in the Hall of Trials on level GF.

Humming Nettles (Japanese: , Hamingu Ooba) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they have black petals that look like musical notes and when they sway someone wants to sing. Two are required for Things that Hum.

Honey Rhubarbs (Japanese: , Makuna Amamitsu) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they are cool, sweet, honey-like foodstuff that most Nopon are crazy about. Four are required for Cook-Off Comeback?.

Hode Planks (Japanese: , Fūdi no Heimen Mokuzai) are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Hyle and Scout Hodes in Makna Forest. Hode Planks are also available via trade. According to their description, they are planks that stay smooth without sanding and there isn't much they can be used for. Five Hode Planks are needed for Bridge Repair, and three more are needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 1,700 Noponstones.
The High Entia Tomb Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in .

Hox Daylight Spurs (Japanese: , Hoggusu no Seiten Hari) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by White Hoxes or Dark Hoxes on platforms below Raguel Bridge on Bionis' Leg, or can be traded for. According to their description, a single one of them grows on a fine day and they are considered a rare biological phenomenon. One is needed for Replica Monado 3, and three for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 7,500 Noponstones.
The High Entia (English dub: ), referred to as the Bird People by Nopon, are a race in .

Hoko (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in . He can be found at the Top Housing Level in Frontier Village, just outside the corridor that leads to an external staircase, all down a level from the Chief's Residence. If he migrates to Colony 6, he has his own tent north of Reconstruction HQ.

Hunger Crashes (Japanese: , Kūfuku Kurasshu) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found Galahad Fortress and Colony 6. According to their description, Reyn named them with satisfaction and they are juicy foods that quickly fill someone up.

The High Entia Tomb (ハイエンター墓所, Haientā Bosho, lit. High Entia Graveyard) is an area in . It is the location of a ceremonial trial; Melia comes here to prove that she is a worthy successor to the throne. It is accessed from Eryth Sea after Melia is announced crown princess.

Humming Cabbages (Japanese: , Hamingu Mekyabeshi, Humming Brussels Sprouts) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh and Colony 6. According to their description, eating one will make someone want to spontaneously start singing. Two are required for Things that Hum.

Hot Taros (Japanese: , Hotto Murasaki Imo, Hot Purple Taro) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they give off steam even when they are raw and they are considered a chef's friend.

High Entia Jewels (Japanese: , Haiento Jueru) are collectables in . They can be found Bionis' Interior and later in Colony 6. They presumably have some connection with the High Entia and Melia named them deferentially.

※ After this quest is completed, Deki may offer another quest. See A Worried Bug-Lover. Hunt for Bug-Loving Friend (Japanese: , Mushisuki Nakama wo Motomete) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Kokora at Nopon Tower in Frontier Village. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Honouring the Nopon Sage (Japanese: , Sennin no Osonae) is a quest in . It can be received from Pipiki in the Central Plaza, west border of the Sacred Altar's pool, in Frontier Village after completing Strange Noises from Below. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment. After completing this quest, Pipiki will offer Meeting the Nopon Sage.

※ After this quest is completed, Kilaki may offer another quest. See Heropon's Spirit. Hunt for a Patron (Japanese: , Patoron wo Sagase) is a quest in . It can be received from Leku in the northeastern area of the Archaeology Level in Frontier Village. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

※ After this quest is completed, Leku may offer another quest. See Beat Kilaki to it!. Heropon's Spirit (Japanese: , Yūsha no Kokoroiki) is a quest in . It can be received from Kilaki in the upper area of the Archaeology Level in Frontier Village. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Humming Plums (Japanese: , Hamingu Puramu) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are plums that make someone who eats them burst into song. Two are required for Things that Hum.

Humming Cats (Japanese: , Hamingu Kyatto) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, they are cats with hot mottled red paws that meow in pleasing harmonies. Two are required for Things that Hum.

High Violets (Japanese: , Hai Vaioretto) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, Melia named them on instinct and they are staves that gather harmful energy.

Ice Kiwi Fruits (Japanese: , Aisu Kiui) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are cool kiwis that clears the head and they can help people to study at night.
Hunter Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be bought at the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg, or be traded for with Don Argentis in Colony 6 or Matryona in the Refugee Camp.
Homs Chestplates are medium torso armour in . They can be bought from the shop at the Refugee Camp for 5,000 G.
Hide Belts are light legs armour in . They are commonly worn by hunters on Gaur Plain.

Hover Shoes are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They were most likely meant to go with the Gravity Stone Band, which have a similar appearance and caption. They are said to be made from the core of a Hovering Reef at Eryth Sea.
Hierax Gloves are light arms armour in . They are said to use feathers of a "phantom bird" in Makna Forest.
Hierax Caps (Japanese: , Hierakusu Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Hierax Tops are light torso armour in . They can be dropped by various enemies and obtained by completing two quests.

The Hidden Machina Village (Japanese: , Mashīna no Kakurega) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of the Fallen Arm. It is a Machina village, where most of the Machina NPCs in the game are found. It is in the palm of the hand of the arm, and is located inside a circle formed by a pipe. There is one location and one landmark in the village; the Ether Light and the Junks, respectively. The Ether Exhaust System is a miniature replica of the village. There are two shops in the village. The first shop initially sells anti-Mechon weapons and art books. After the events of the Meyneth Shrine, the first shop's inventory changes and a second shop opens. It sells Mechonis Armour and art
Homs Military Caps (Japanese: , Homusu no Gunbō) are medium head armour in . They are the official issue of the Homs army.
Hunter Gear (Japanese: , Hantā Gia) is medium head armour in .
Hoxes (Japanese: , Hoggusu) are a family of squirrel-like enemies in the . They have no appearance change between games, and come in brown and white varieties.
Hunter Gauntlets are medium arms armour in . They can be dropped by Black Flamii.
Homs Gauntlets are medium arms armour in . They are the official issue of the Homs army.

The Hode Lair (Japanese: , Fūdi no Sumika) is a location in . It is located in Makna Forest, at the southeast corner of the map, just south of Precipice Bridge. To enter the lair, which is barred by a wooden door, Kilaki's Note must be obtained from Heropon's Spirit. In the subsequent quest Beat Kilaki to it!, the Obsessive Galgaron, a Level 35 Unique Monster, must be defeated.
Hunter Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for with Olga.
Ice Climbing Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Homs Military Boots are medium feet armour in . They are used by the Homs army.
Hunter Boots are medium feet armour in . They can be dropped by Brave Tirkins.

The Hidden Warehouse (Japanese: , Kakushi Sōko) is a location in . It is a part of the Mag Mell Ruins in Tephra Cave, although it cannot be accessed until after the events at the Mechonis Core, and is inhabited by the Unique Monster Reckless Galdon. It can be reached by following the small passage on the north side of Tephra Cavern, or by jumping down the small hole just north of the the Heavenly Window, which lands the party in the Forgotten Cave, and then following the path to the east.

I Want to be a Homs! (Japanese: , Homusu ni Naritai) is a quest in . It can be received from Rakzet, who can be found near the connected land southwest of the Junks in the Hidden Machina Village. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.
Hode Attack (Japanese: , Fūdi wo Gekitaiseyo) is a quest in . It is received from Jarack at the Ether Plant in the Eryth Sea, once Trouble at the Plant has been completed.
Hunting Knives (Japanese: , Hantānaifu) are weapons in . They are Fiora's starting knives, and can only be acquired otherwise through trade in Colony 9.
Horizons (Japanese: , Suiten'ippeki) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban. It can be obtained by purchasing it at the Syrath Lighthouse Shop for 27,300 G.
The Hurricane Shot (Japanese: , Harikēnshotto) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is an ether rifle wielded by Sharla.

Hunting Nibblers (Japanese: , Tankyū no Bakubaku, Searching Nibbler) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. They can be obtained by purchasing it at the Melfica Road Shop for 13,800 G as well as trading with Rozeal or Jarack in Alcamoth and Eryth Sea respectively. Hunting Nibblers take on the shape of a lion's head with a grey colouration.
The Hunter Biter (Japanese: , Karyūdo no Kamukamu) is one of Riki's biters in . It is Riki's starting weapon, and can otherwise only be obtained through trading.
Hrunting (Japanese: , Furuntingu) are Unique weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are twin blades wielded by Fiora.

High Entia Souls (Japanese: , Haientosouru) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staffs that can be wielded by Melia. As a Unique Weapon, it is similar to Riki's Banquet Biter, giving the player three free gems with which to improve status effects.
Hierax Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made from the feathers of a "phantom bird" in Makna Forest.
The High Entia Medicine is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It must be found for Mislabelling Problem, and is dropped by the Abominable Hiln at Showdown Cliff in Eryth Sea.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. How Do They Feel (Japanese: , Kimochi wo Shiritai) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Scarlen at the Main Entrance of Alcamoth. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. How Do I Feel? (Japanese: , Jibun no Honshin wo Shiritai) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Scarlen at the Main Entrance of Alcamoth. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Hodes (Japanese: , Fūdi, lit. Hoody) are an enemy family in and . They are small humanoid creatures with long cloaks and glowing eyes. They are found in Makna Forest and Eryth Sea. They seem to employ Orlugas as workers or fighters and can sometimes be seen riding them. The behaviour, adornments and social structure of Hodes strongly suggest they are an intelligent race, but they can still be harmed by the Monado unlike the Homs, Nopon and High Entia.

The High Entia Emblem is a Key Item in . It is obtained by completing The Imperial Ceremony in Satorl Marsh, consisting of collecting four Radiants, offering them on the Adulthood Emblem in front of the Sororal Statues and defeating the Radiant Pterix. It opens sealed High Entia Doors throughout Bionis, and the Sororal Statues lift.

The High Entia Doors are special places in . They are located throughout Bionis, and are marked with a distinctive symbol, the Ancient Insignia. They cannot be opened until the seal on them is unlocked by the High Entia Emblem, which can be obtained by completing The Imperial Ceremony and Imperial Ceremony Offerings.
The Hode Ponytail is a rare material item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be obtained by various hodes around Eryth Sea, and can also be traded for.
Hypnotise (Japanese: , Surīpumaindo, Sleep Mind) is one of Melia's Ether arts in and . It cause a target to fall asleep temporarily.

The Hope Farm (Japanese: , Kibō no Nōjō) is a location in . It is located east of the Main Entrance to Colony 6. The northern entrance to the Hope Farm (south of Watchpoint Junction) is locked off until the Ether Mine is escaped, and the southern entrance (north of the Pod Depot) can only be reached after the same point. The Demon King Dragonia is fought here. There are two Heart-to-Hearts here: "Dunban's Right Arm" and "Recovery and Reflection".

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. I Love You No Matter What (Japanese: , Nanigaattemo Kimi wo Aisu) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Scarlen at the Main Entrance of Alcamoth. Scarlen asks the party to deliver his letter to Ricoth. This quest is triggered by talking to Ricoth first (A route) then to Rozeal in How Do I Feel?. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment. This quest and Together Forever are mutually exclusive. The route choice made during How Do I Feel? determines which quest will be available.

Hode Camouflages are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Hodes in Makna Forest, or traded for. According to their description, they are worn to blend in with the forest and they stink, but washing them kills the effect. Three are needed for Strange Noises from Below.

Hiln Coin Purses are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Hilns in Eryth Sea and traded for. According to their description, they could be used to carry change although there is a hole in them. Three are required to complete Collect Quest 1 in Eryth Sea.

Hyle Hodes are enemies in . They are members of the Hode family, and can be found at level 31 - 33 in the Abyss Basin, on Precipice Bridge, and in the Hode Lair in Makna Forest. They can drop the Hode Planks needed for Bridge Repair and Colony 6 Reconstruction.
Hiln (Japanese: , Hirun) are a family of bird enemies in the . They are uncommon and look like seagulls with purple glowing orbs attached to their faces. There is no appearance change between and .

I Will Never Forget You (Japanese: , Anata wo Wasurenai) is a quest in . It can be received from Vidian at the Ether Plant in Eryth Sea, after she is rescued from Whitewing Palace in Alcamoth during Vidian Rescue Mission. This quest can be obtained if Believing Again has been completed before the events at Mechonis Core. Otherwise, the party will obtain The Only Thing I Can Do, since both quests are mutually exclusive. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment.

The Hungry Volff (Japanese: , Garō no Vorufu) is a one-of-a-kind quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Volff family, and can be found at level 33 in Satorl Marsh on a ledge east of the Glowing Obelisk. It will drop a Fancy Volff Hide, three of which are needing for Making Camp. The Hungry Volff only appears during the quest What is Courage?!. Completing the quest requires defeating either the Hungry Volff or Elegant Marin. If Elegant Marin is defeated first, it is not possible to fight the Hungry Volff during the same play-through.

Hovering Reef 1 (Japanese: , Dai 1 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Latael Shore, Showdown Cliff and Hovering Reef 2. Mir'leiz is found here during Bring Back My Son!.

Hovering Reef 4 (Japanese: , Dai 4 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reefs 3, 5 and 7, and is the location of the Syrath Lighthouse.

Hovering Reef 2 (Japanese: , Dai 2 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reefs 1 and 3, as well as the Centre Gate. A Heart-to-Heart, "Flowers of Eryth Sea", is located here.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in the High Entia Tomb.
Hovering Reef 6 (Japanese: , Dai 6 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reef 5 and the Ether Crystal Deposit.

Hot Selua Cells are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from the Officer Robusto and Chimai Selua in Bionis' Interior. Hot Selua Cells are not otherwise obtainable. According to their description, they are cells that are hot like magma and are considered the saviour of people lost in the snow.

The Highmore Caviar is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is made by dipping Red Pollen Orbs into the Shining Pond in Satorl Marsh, as instructed by Zazadan during A Mysterious Delicacy. It must then be delivered to Dedeba during A Gift?

The Hidden Machina Village Shop 1 is a shop in . It is located in the Hidden Machina Village on Fallen Arm. It is manned by a male Machina. It specialises in Mechonis Armour and anti-Mechon weapons, which do not require Topple or Monado Enchant to damage Mechon. After the events at the Meyneth Shrine, the first shop will change its inventory, and will focus on Homs weapons and armour. A second shop will open as well, selling only Mechonis Armour. __TOC__ Note: In the following tables, "before MSE" or "after MSE" means the item is only available before or after completing the Meyneth Shrine events.

The Hope Farm Shop is a shop in . It is run by a female Nopon Merchant, who initially resides at Watchpoint Junction, outside the gate to Colony 6 near Daza. After the liberation of Colony 6, she moves to the entrance to Hope Farm. The shop is accessible day and night. After the Mechonis Core events (Chapter 17), the shop expands its selection with Mechonis-sourced weapons and armour. It also drops a couple of old items. __TOC__ Note: In the following tables, "MC" refers to the events in Mechonis Core.

High Entia History (Japanese: , Kodai Haientā no Ibutsu, Remains of the Ancient High Entia) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh, between Dunban and Melia at purple affinity.

Hopes and Plans (Japanese: , Kibō no Zento, A Hopeful Outlook) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Hall of Trials in the High Entia Tomb, between Melia and Shulk at pink affinity. It can only be viewed after the events at Mechonis Core.

Hometown (故郷) is a Field Track in , composed and arranged by Yoko Shimomura. It is track 1 of disc 3 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is heard during the day in the districts of the Colony 9 town proper: the Commercial, Military, and Residential Districts. In , Hometown is used as a music motif for "Yesterdale - Colony 9", the track that plays when the party is in Colony 9.

Hope (希望（ゲーム中未使用）, Hope (unused in game)) is the sole Bonus Track in , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 6 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This is the only music from the album that, as its parenthetical soundtrack title suggests, does not play in the original version of the game. However, it does play in later versions of the game. * In , it can be found in the Jukebox as a Bonus Track to be unlocked after completing the game. * In , a version of the song plays during the Quiet Moment "Light and Shadow".
The Hidden Machina Village Shop 2 is a shop in . It opens up in the Hidden Machina Village after the events at the Meyneth Shrine. It focuses on Mechonis Armour and art books.
Hovering Reef 3 (Japanese: , Dai 3 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reefs 2 and 4.
Highland Lepyxes (Japanese: , Hairando Fontera) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Lepyx family, and can be found at level 49 at Seaswept Rise in Primordia.

Howard is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Human who can be found at the Central Industrial District of New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Curators Division. He is the pilot of the titular vehicle in the mission A Proper Chopper. During this mission, he can be found at Sunlit Spring in Noctilum.
Higher Ground is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character is above the enemy.
Hydro Forfexes (Japanese: , Haidoro Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 31-35 at Sayram Lake in Primordia.

Huge Potamuses (Japanese: , Masu Hippo, Mass Hippo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Potamus family, and can be found at level 21-22 at east Sayram Lake, level 21-24 at northeast Janpath Lake, and level 29-30 near west Biahno Lake in Primordia.
Hunter Grexes (Japanese: , Hantā Rupusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Grex family, and can be found at level 22-30 at Cliffside Camp in Oblivia.
Hushed Murras (Japanese: , Kurausu Tondomu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Murra family, and can be found at level 11-15 in Sylvalum.
Highland Jaculs (Japanese: , Hairando Hasutara) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Jacul family, and can be found at level 55 near Delusians South Summit in Sylvalum.

Hummingstones (Japanese: , Hanautasutōn) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular the northeast portion on the path headed toward Oblivia. One is needed for Definian Love.

The Hilal Stronghold (Japanese: , Hirāru Yōsai) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion base located in Sylvalum, southeast of the Hilal Meadow. It is mostly inhabited by Marnuck, and several Important Items can be found here; Cockpit Wreckage during Waste Not, Want Not, Med Kits during A Challenger Approaches and the Zirtodiamond during The Old Gods. The FN Site 409 is located here.

The Humdrum Peaks (Japanese: , Muji Sanchi) are an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a flat plain located in Noctilum, north of the Garden Spring and southwest of Tripod Rock, which is laden with hidden low-level Tectinsulas. The Solar Starship Map can be found here during Proficiency Exam 4, and Satsu can be found here during Missing in Action.

Ian Parker (Japanese: , Ian) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Water Purification Plant in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. After Water Woes is completed, he can be found at the Biahno Water-Purification Plant in Primordia, until Lakeside Getaway is accepted. He is a staff member of the Biahno water-purification plant and works as the "Miran Hydrology Team Lead".

Hunter Diluses (Japanese: , Hantā Kurogosu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Dilus family. They can be found at level 60 at the southern part of Divine Roost in Noctilum.
Horned Helmets (Japanese: , Rasshuheddo) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.

High Accelerators (Japanese: , Haiakuserarēta) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia near Talon Rock Second Terrane. Seven are needed for the Basic Mission A Repairman's Resolve.
Hope Springs Eternal (Japanese: , NLA no Seijo, The Saintess of NLA) is an Affinity Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received at the Cathedral in the Residential District.
Hexagauges (Japanese: , Ōvahekisa) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Four of them are needed for Xenotech Survey.
Honey Papils (Japanese: , Hanī Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 9-10 near South Janpath BC in Primordia at daytime.
Icarus Wings (Japanese: , Patapata Ōzubasa) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.

Hugo (Japanese: , Fūgo) is a NPC in . He can be found at the Integrated Production Plant or at the back of the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles. He offers a series of missions to create Battle Probes.
Holmium Petramands (Japanese: , Horumiumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family and can be found at level 56-58 in Rockmole's Burrow in Noctilum.

Holofigures are items in . They can be displayed on any one of five holofigure projectors in the BLADE Barracks after the player reaches BLADE Level 2 in the Wii U version, or by default in the . Holofigures are classed in Weapons, Armor, Enemies and Special. These can be acquired through defeating storyline Bosses or Tyrants and completing Missions or Collectopedia rows. As the Wii U online servers have shut down, the Yggralith Zero and Phanatos Holofigures are now unobtainable. However, the Neilnail Albus and Neilnail Furvus Holofigures are still obtainable from the Time Attack Missions.
Hilal Meadow (Japanese: , Hirāru Heigen) is a landmark in . It is an open plain located in Sylvalum, southeast of the Needle Rock Sandsea and northeast of the Hilal Stronghold.

Hiro, the Priceless (Japanese: , Ōsui no Hiiro) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Blatta family. It can be found at level 66-70 at Sandsprint Cavity in Sylvalum during nighttime. It is a Hidden Enemy, crawling on one of the greenish crystals in the southwest corner near the cave's floor.

The High-Output Pugilith (Japanese: , Shutsuryoku Kyōka-gata Berudero) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Pugilith machine. It can be found at level 47 at the spiraling ledge leading down to Badr Stronghold in Sylvalum. It can drop the New Cylinders needed for It's-a Mia!.
The Hot Dog is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is needed as a bargaining tool with Aganeba during the course of The Pip-Squeak.

Hrym Blattas (Japanese: , Furyumu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 31-40 in Cauldros's Titan's Table or east of FN Site 502.
High Tension is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Enforcer at rank 10.

I <3 Pizza is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a female Ma-non carrying a stack of several pizzas. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Murder Most Foul.

Human-Made Skells (Japanese: , Dōru) are machine enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Skell enemies made from Human technology. They are all Mission Exclusive enemies, including one Boss. With one exception, they are all Urban models.
Hulking Incisors are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Huge Potamuses in Primordia or traded for 30 Reward Tickets. One is needed for Gorkwa Games.

Hi-Spec Sensor Modules are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Zigs in Sylvalum or traded for 54 Reward Tickets. One is needed for Gorkwa Games. They are needed to craft the Skell weapon augments Custom.WP-FUEL.

Horonalderon (Japanese: , Horon'arudehiron) is an NPC in and . They are a Zaruboggan, and after Dead Men Tell No Tales can be found near Repenta Diner in the Industrial District. After completing their mission The Good Thief, Horonalderon can be found in the Central Industrial District.

Honey Oils are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from orange Ciniculas in Primordia. They can also be redeemed using 114 Reward Tickets. One unit of Honey Oil is required during The Handy Ma-non.

Howitzer Barrager Zigs (Japanese: , Hauzābaretto Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 31-40 in the O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins near O'rrh Sim Gate in Cauldros.

Howitzer Gunner Zigs (Japanese: , Hauzākyanon Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 45 on the Northern Searoad in Sylvalum, due west of the fast travel point.

Howitzer Launcher Zigs (Japanese: , Hauzāranchā Jigu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Zig machines, and can be found at level 59 at Cavernous Abyss, and at level 60 on a wall southeast of the Northern Searoad fast travel point, Arc Rock, the entrance to Quay Hollows, Delusians South Summit, and on an arch above FN Site 401 in Sylvalum.
The Ice Cream Cake is a material in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be obtained from the Oc-serv Seivo in Sylvalum during Predator and Prey if "Fight" is chosen during the second objective.

House Call (Japanese: , Ijū niyoru Eikyō, Impacts of Migration) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Nan'celeg in the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship. Although not a prerequisite, the Basic Mission Under the Weather can be used to locate this mission.

Hyper Railgun! is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located near the Integrated Production Plant in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles between Alexa and Cross in the early morning.

Homer is an Human NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Biahno Water-Purification Plant in Primordia during The Good Thief. After the mission, he cannot be encountered anymore as he was arrested and sent in prison.

Ian's ID Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is found on the body of the defeated Raging Cantor at the Primordia's Biahno Water-Purification Plant during Lakeside Getaway and is used to access security camera audio recorded during the attack on the water purification plant.
The Hexad-Partican is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is known as Six-Cannon in the Japanese version.
Hidden Cantor Hoards are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Cantors. One is needed for The Jewelmonger (Hidden Cantor Hoard).

Hungry Auravises (Japanese: , Hangurī Akuira) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Auravis family, and are fought at level 11-14 on the North Janpath Plain in Primordia during Muimui's Meltdown.
Hexuna Nebra is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Tree Clan Prone and can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles at night. She is Bazis Wolfen's wife.

Hot Potamus Juice are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from red Potamuses, or for 30 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in I and V Ultrafauna Criticals Up, Ultrafauna Slayer, CriticalUp.ULTRAFAUNA, and Slayer.ULTRAFAUNA augments.

beside an unassuming rock formation]] Hidden Enemies are a type of enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are not a particular family but rather those that use a particular mechanic - being hidden from the party. This means that they cannot be targeted, will not appear on the mini-map, and will attack the party regardless of level if approached. Some families of enemy are always hidden, although most can be hidden or not hidden. Often members of the same sub-group of enemy will appear in the same area, some hidden and others not. Hidden enemies tend to resemble either natural features or inactive machines; they often appear partially submerged in the ground or hanging from the roofs of caves.
Hot Dogs = Happy is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts two Ma-non sharing a hot dog. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Emotion Commotion.

Honor Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Factory 1.21 Shield. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Professorial. The Honor weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Honor * Iron Honor * Carbide Honor * Cermet Honor * Chrome Honor * Chromoly Honor * Cobalt Honor * Titanium Honor * Ceramic Honor * Diamond Honor

Hunting the Headless is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.1, and is unlocked if the final Vesper's tail is broken during The Vesper Nest. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Hidden Threats is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.8, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eighteen Adseculas. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

High-Profile Target is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.11, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty Milsaadis. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Hot Pursuit is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.15, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting five Vilem, the Gold-Scaled. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Hunting License is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.19, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting six Apricas. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Hunter Hunting is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.20, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twelve Vigents. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Humanoids (Japanese: , Eirian, Alien) are a category of enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It includes all living, non-human enemies that have the same general body plan as humans, with a head, two arms, two legs, and an upright stance. All enemy xenoforms belong to this category, along with the only two Miran Sylooth and Gularth races, the others all belonging to Ganglion or Samaarian factions. All regular Humanoids resist Ether-based attacks, and possess a weakness to Beam damage, with Tyrants usually having 5 extra resistance against every attribute, and bosses having completely unique resistances.
High Danger Surge is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that increases the chance of triggering the HP Peril Soul Voice.
Humanoid Criticals Up is a ground weapon critical Augment in and that increases critical chance when attacking Humanoid-classified enemies. The Skell equivalent is CriticalUp.HUMANOID.
Humanoid Slayer is a ground weapon enemy exploit Augment in and that increases damage dealt to Humanoid-classified enemies. The Skell equivalent is Slayer.HUMANOID.

Hope's Bodywear is Casual Wear upper body armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Hope's initial gear when she is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way. It is one of the few pieces of Casual Wear to have a level requirement.

The Hyde Dyads are a one-of-a-kind ranged weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Dual Guns. They are acquired during the Normal Mission That's In-Credible! and must be used to defeat the chosen enemies. They must be returned to Tutura after the enemies have been defeated. This weapon cannot be sold, nor can any augment slots be added to them.
Hope's Legwear is Light Wear leg armor in and . It is manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. It is part of Hope's initial gear when she is recruited, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Hoodies are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
High-Spec Scouters are Casual Wear Head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.

Hit Points, commonly referred to as HP, are an important mechanic in and . They are needed to keep characters from being incapacitated. If the controlled character has 0 HP, the AI characters must use a party bar to revive the incapacitated character. If there is no party bar or no battle, the party will be transported back to the last landmark they visited. During the time between battles, HP are recovered quickly. Outside battle, if a character has an Auto-Heal Up gem equipped, their HP will recover more quickly. HP values are influenced by multiple factors: * Taking damage from enemy attacks * Taking spike damage * Taking damage from status effects (Poison, Chill, Burn, and Bleed) * Being

Hirkham is an Ardainian in . He can be found at the Goldmouth Return Port in the Argentum Trade Guild. Paying him the 15 Gold mooring fee in Chapter 1 counts towards Perun's Level 2 "Key Affinity Reward". Hirkham originally hails from the Empire of Mor Ardain, but moved to Argentum due to the combination of work opportunities and failure to join the Ardainian army. At some point, he attempted to resonate with a Core Crystal but lacked the aptitude, and he was rendered unconscious for five days.
Hide and Seek (Japanese: , Kakurenbo) is a quest in . It can be received from Aft in Bower Lounge in the Argentum Trade Guild.

Hold #1 (Japanese: , Daiichi Sōko) is a location in . It is a large room in the Ancient Ship, directly below the Ship Bridge, Mid-Deck and above Hold #2. There are two Treasure Troves here, and a section of floor which will collapse when walked across.
Hold #2 (Japanese: , Daini Sōko) is a location in . It is a large room in the Ancient Ship, directly below Hold #1 and before the Loading Bay. There is a Treasure Trove here.
Honeycomb Sweets (Japanese: , Suītsu Hanī Shiroppu) is a shop in . It is run by Bonbon and can be found in the Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild. It is specialized in Desserts.
Hydro Blast (Japanese: , Haidoroburasuto) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Catalyst Scimitar. It shoots ahead in a straight line, and causes Knockback.

The Honeypot Grotto (Japanese: , Sukīto no Su) is a location in . It is located in the right area of the upper level of the Gormott Province, as a small enclave near the north exit to the left area. Collection Points of this location can provide Melosian Honey needed for the quest The Militia's Request. The Unique Monster Immovable Gonzalez can be found on a ledge directly above the grotto. Dahlia's Heart-to-Heart, "The Purest Beauty?", can be found here.

The Holy Gate of Fontana (Japanese: , Fontāna Daiseimon) is a Landmark in . It is located at the Sevind Palace Plaza of Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. This place leads to the Olethro Ruins and the Ruins of Fountain Park.
Hope's Horizon (Japanese: , Nozomi no Gankai) is a landmark in . It is located on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal, between the Twin Pillars and Sekis Pillar.

Highway 8 (Japanese: , Dai-8 Kōsokudōro) is a location in . It is located on the Streets of the Land of Morytha, accessible by climbing the Fallen Skyscraper. From here, the Secret Area View of a Lost Time can be reached by knocking down a signpost and walking up it and climbing up the Genome Center. There are several Treasure Troves here, including one containing the Robolab Club Quarterly.

The Hill Overlooking Elysium (Japanese: , Rakuen wo Miorosu Oka) is a landmark in . It is located on the Upper Level of the First Low Orbit Station, in Elysium, and is accessed from the Rhadamanthus Portal. There are no enemies here.
The Hot Pipe District, 1F (Japanese: , Hainetsu Kanku 1-kai) is a Landmark in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain.
